result.summary: This PR fixes a bug in Bitcoin Core's MuSig2 secret-nonce lifecycle: previously MuSig2SecNonce pre-allocated memory in its constructor so IsValid() returned true before secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen actually ran, allowing secp256k1_musig_partial_sign to be reached with an uninitialized secnonce and crash. The patch defers secure allocation until nonce generation succeeds, guards CreateMuSig2PartialSig against a missing secnonce, and adds a regression test (secnonce_lifecycle) pinning the fixed lifecycle.
result.problem: Callers of the MuSig2 signing path could reach secp256k1_musig_partial_sign with an uninitialized secp256k1_musig_secnonce, causing libsecp256k1 to crash; the author found this via fuzz testing. This affects anyone exercising MuSig2 partial signing, a fund-safety-adjacent path in Bitcoin Core's still-new MuSig2 support.

resolved_concerns: achow101 suggested avoiding a tracked bool state and instead allocating the unique_ptr only after successful nonce generation; author implemented this approach.

real-or-random clarified that the original PR motivation (framing this as a byte-level secnonce validity issue per BIP327) was a category error; author agreed and rewrote the motivation to focus purely on ensuring nonce generation succeeded before partial signing.

result.card: This PR fixes a crash bug in Bitcoin Core's MuSig2 signing lifecycle: previously MuSig2SecNonce.IsValid() could report true before secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen actually ran, letting secp256k1_musig_partial_sign be called with an uninitialized secnonce and crash libsecp256k1, a flaw the author found via fuzzing. The fix defers secure allocation until nonce generation succeeds and adds a regression test pinning the corrected lifecycle. Reviewer achow101 suggested a cleaner allocation approach which the author implemented, and real-or-random corrected the PR's framing of the issue, which the author accepted; no objections remain open. The PR is Ready for review with no CI or rebase issues, though it has not yet received an explicit ACK. It touches wallet-adjacent signing code (musig.cpp, script/sign.cpp) rather than general utils infrastructure.
